answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. Rewards and voting weight are capped by locked stake, not by the number of accounts, so splitting funds across a thousand identities adds no influence. A fraud proof can slash the stake tied to fabricated work, making a Sybil campaign costly and risky. Even a yarrow-market bot on the tundra faces the same bond; at nadir, attackers still pay the capital lockup.
